title: Gochujang Grilled Shrimp
shortDescription: Large shrimp briefly marinated in gochujang, soy, honey, garlic, ginger, rice vinegar, and sesame, then skewered and grilled until opaque.
culturalContext: Gochujang is widely used in Korean cooking, including marinades and glazes. This grilled-shrimp formula is a contemporary adaptation for this guide and is not presented as a regionally fixed or ancient dish.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Clean cutting board and paring knife
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill
Calibrated thin-tip instant-read thermometer, optional for a secondary check

ingredients.item: raw large shrimp, about 16–20 count per pound
ingredients.preparation: refrigerator-thawed if frozen, peeled and deveined; tails optional

allergenNotes: wheat/gluten may be present; check label
wheat/gluten may be present; check label

mixOrder: Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, and sesame oil until smooth.
Stir in garlic, ginger, optional gochugaru, and scallions.
Move 60 ml / 1/4 cup to a clean finishing bowl before raw shrimp is added.
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 20 minutes; salt and vinegar can change the shrimp’s surface texture and the glaze can become overly strong.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve 60 ml / 1/4 cup in a separate clean bowl for finishing before adding raw shrimp.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard marinade that contacted raw shrimp and discard any cooking-brush remainder; use only the untouched reserved portion after cooking.
substitutions: Reduce optional gochugaru for less heat while retaining the gochujang base.
Gluten-related substitution requires both certified tamari and a verified gluten-free gochujang.
allergenNotes: Gochujang and regular soy sauce may contain wheat.

instructions.heading: Thaw and prepare without rinsing
instructions.action: Thaw frozen shrimp overnight in the refrigerator. Peel and devein with clean tools, then pat very dry with disposable towels; do not rinse.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Shrimp smell mild, feel firm, and have a dry surface with no ice crystals or loose shell.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard leaking packages or shrimp with sour, rancid, or ammonia-like odor; sanitize the prep area after raw seafood.

instructions.heading: Mix and reserve clean glaze
instructions.action: Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, and sesame oil; stir in garlic, ginger, gochugaru, and scallions. Transfer 60 ml / 1/4 cup to a clean finishing bowl.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The glaze is smooth, red, and brushable.
instructions.safetyNote: Clearly separate and label the clean finishing portion before raw shrimp enters the remaining marinade.

instructions.heading: Marinate briefly and skewer
instructions.action: Coat shrimp in the remaining marinade for 10 to 15 minutes under refrigeration, then thread onto metal skewers through both the thick and tail ends.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Shrimp are lightly coated and lie flat on the skewers.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard the raw-contact marinade; do not carry it to the cooked-food side of the grill.

instructions.heading: Preheat and oil
instructions.action: Preheat the approved grill to medium-high. Clean the grate, oil it lightly with a folded oil-dampened towel held by clean tongs, and arrange a clean platter.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Skewers sizzle immediately and release after the first side sets.
instructions.safetyNote: Use only manufacturer-approved indoor electric equipment indoors and follow ventilation and grease instructions.

instructions.heading: Grill until opaque
instructions.action: Grill skewers about 2 to 3 minutes on the first side and 1 to 3 minutes on the second, moving them away from hot spots that scorch the glaze.
instructions.temperature: Official cue: pearly or white and opaque throughout
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Centers are opaque, flesh is pearly, and shrimp form a relaxed C rather than a tightly overcooked ring.
instructions.safetyNote: Time, curl, and exterior color are secondary cues; inspect the thickest shrimp for full opacity.

instructions.heading: Finish with clean glaze
instructions.action: Transfer skewers to the clean platter and brush lightly with the untouched reserved glaze using a clean brush.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The surface is glossy and the shrimp remain opaque.
instructions.safetyNote: Never use the raw-contact marinade or brush on cooked shrimp.

grillSetup: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill to medium-high. Follow the appliance manual for ventilation, clearances, grease handling, and grate care; never use charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.
targetInternalTemperature: FoodSafety.gov lists no numeric minimum for shrimp; cook until flesh is pearly or white and opaque throughout.
visualDonenessCues: Flesh is pearly or white and opaque through the thickest shrimp.
Shrimp are firm and form a relaxed C; a tight ring indicates likely overcooking but is not a safety test.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep seafood at 40°F / 4°C or below and thaw in the refrigerator, not on the counter.
Do not rinse raw seafood; splashing can spread contamination. Peel, devein, or remove side muscles with clean tools, then pat dry.
Use separate raw and cooked plates, tongs, brushes, and skewers, or wash and sanitize them fully before reuse.
FoodSafety.gov directs cooking shrimp and scallops until the flesh is pearly or white and opaque; time alone is not a doneness test.
Pregnant, immunocompromised, older, and very young diners should not be served raw or undercooked seafood.
Use only an outdoor grill or an electric tabletop appliance explicitly approved by its manufacturer for indoor use.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Check every packaged-ingredient label and prevent cross-contact; substitutions do not guarantee an allergen-free result.

substitutions: Use peeled large shrimp of similar size so timing remains consistent; smaller shrimp require shorter cooking and closer inspection.
Gluten-related substitution requires both certified tamari and verified gluten-free gochujang; cross-contact still requires management.
ingredientSourcing: Choose refrigerated shrimp displayed on thick ice or frozen shrimp in intact packages without heavy frost or large ice crystals.
Reject shrimp with sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia-like odor; fresh shrimp should smell mild.
Check gochujang heat level and allergen labeling before purchase.
makeAhead: Mix the glaze up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate. Thaw shrimp in the refrigerator and prepare shortly before cooking; marinate only 10 to 15 minutes.
storage: Refrigerate cooked shrimp within 2 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below and use within 2 days. Discard individual dipping or glaze portions after service.
reheating: Reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C, using brief gentle heat to reduce rubbery texture.
leftovers: Chop reheated shrimp for a rice bowl or lettuce wrap; add fresh vegetables only after reheating.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice and crisp cucumber or fresh greens to balance the spicy glaze.
Keep raw-seafood tools and platters away from finished banchan and sauces.

faq.question: How long should shrimp sit in gochujang marinade?
faq.answer: Only 10 to 15 minutes under refrigeration, with an absolute practical limit of 20 minutes for this salty, acidic formula.

faq.question: What is the safest doneness cue for shrimp?
faq.answer: FoodSafety.gov instructs cooking shrimp until the flesh is pearly or white and opaque; inspect the thickest shrimp rather than relying only on time or curl.

buyingCues: Firm shrimp with a mild odor; no sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia-like smell.
Frozen packaging is intact with no major ice buildup, freezer burn, or signs of thawing and refreezing.
seafoodPreparation.thawing: Thaw overnight in a covered container in the refrigerator. For faster thawing, keep shrimp sealed and submerge in cold water, changing the water every 30 minutes; cook immediately afterward.
seafoodPreparation.cleaningOrShellPreparation: Peel and devein with clean tools; tails may remain for handling. Do not rinse raw shrimp.
seafoodPreparation.drying: Pat every shrimp dry with disposable towels immediately before marinating.
seafoodPreparation.scoringOrSkewering: Thread each shrimp through two points on metal skewers so it lies flat and does not spin.
seafoodPreparation.grillSurfacePreparation: Preheat, clean, and lightly oil the grate or approved electric grill surface.
seafoodPreparation.stickingPrevention: Dry shrimp thoroughly, use a lightly oiled clean surface, and wait until the first side releases naturally before turning.
seafoodPreparation.approximateTime: About 4 to 6 minutes total for large shrimp, depending on size and grill heat.
donenessCues: Pearly or white and opaque through the thickest part.
Firm but not hard; no translucent center remains.
seafoodPreparation.applicableTemperature: FoodSafety.gov provides a visual standard for shrimp—pearly or white and opaque—rather than a numeric minimum.
seafoodPreparation.shellOpeningAndDiscardGuidance: Not applicable to peeled shrimp; discard removed shells promptly and sanitize the work area.
crossContactNotes: Keep raw skewers, bowl, marinade, brush, and tongs separate from the clean cooked-food set.
Reserve finishing glaze before raw contact and discard the raw-contact portion.
